title: pointerDelta
description: How far the pointer moved, with no position. Game mode only: a 3D game hides and re-centres the cursor every frame and reads the mouse as relative motion (raw input / DirectInput), so an absolute pointerMove is read as a jump from the centre on every frame and the camera spins. The host injects this as a relative move, the kind a physical mouse produces. The second delta on the channel after scroll, and safe for the same reason: deltas commute, so the host applies every one it receives in whatever order, and a lost one costs that much travel and nothing else -- exactly what a real mouse loses when a packet drops. The only ordering the host enforces is against ABSOLUTE samples: a delta older than the newest pointerMove (or button transition) is dropped, so a packet from before a mode switch cannot nudge a freshly anchored cursor. Coalesced by the sender to at most one per animation frame, deltas summed.

seq.description: Same stream as every other pointer message (pointerSample.schema.json). Deltas are not gated against each other, only against absolute samples.

t.description: Sender's clock in ms. Diagnostics only.

dx.description: Horizontal travel as a fraction of the frame, positive right. Fractions rather than pixels for the same reason positions are: the phone never learns the desktop resolution, and the host scales against the display it is injecting into. One full frame width of travel is 1.0; the bound is generous and exists only to refuse a hostile sender.

dy.description: Vertical travel, same basis as dx, positive down.

buttons.description: Buttons held after this event, as on every pointer message, so a lost pointerUp still repairs itself while the user holds right mouse to aim.
